column1: # The 3E/4E end-code table. One row per code; the EXCEPTION CLASS NAMES are hand-written
# public API in aslmp/errors/__init__.py and are referenced here by name, because people
# put them in except clauses and generated class names drift.
# tools/gen_endcodes.py turns this file into aslmp/errors/endcodes.py as a committed
# literal mapping. Nothing parses a TSV at run time, and the error path in particular
# An empty exception_class means the code has no dedicated subclass and raises the base
# SlmpEndCodeError carrying this row's text. A code that is NOT in this table still
# raises a named class -- SlmpEndCodeError with description 'undocumented end code', the
# code formatted 0x%04X, and a line asking for a report naming the CPU model and
# firmware. Never a bare integer, never a stringified decimal.
# On the wire the end code is little-endian in binary (0xC059 goes out as 59 C0) and
# four upper-case hex characters in ASCII.
# provenance=live rows were observed on the named CPU and firmware. Three of them are
# CORRECTIONS to what the manuals led us to expect (0xC05C, 0xC052, 0xC061) and their
# notes say what the doc-derived mapping predicted, because the point of citing sources
# is to be able to see where they were wrong.
